textile.name: bag
textile.title: bag
textile.reason: This is a classic Karen woven shoulder bag with striped cotton weave and fringed ends, a well-known traditional Karen textile/bag form.

textile.name: cloth
textile.title: cloth
textile.reason: Black cotton cloth with a geometric embroidered grid in red/white/orange thread accented with Job's tears seed beading, a well-documented Karen textile technique and motif style. The museum credits this directly to Karen production, consistent with the visual evidence.

textile.name: väv, fabric
textile.title: väv, fabric
textile.reason: The image shows a handwoven textile with warp-ikat diamond motifs in rust/brown tones on a striped ground with dark bands — consistent with Karen (and related Thai-Myanmar hill-tribe) weaving traditions; the museum's own note attributes it to the Karen people.

textile.name: blanket; hood
textile.title: blanket; hood
textile.reason: A striped, fringed length of handwoven cloth (folded/sewn as blanket or hood) attributed by the museum to Karen makers; striped cotton weaving of this kind is a well-known Karen textile tradition.

textile.name: hanging
textile.title: hanging
textile.reason: A blue cotton woven hanging with supplementary-weft banded patterning, fringe, and bamboo-rod tube top, explicitly made for the tourist market by Karen weavers per the museum's attribution — consistent with known Karen textile production.

household.name: betel-box
household.title: betel-box
household.reason: The image shows a lacquered cane/basketry betel box with banded decoration, a well-known Karen household object confirmed by the museum's production attribution to the Karen.

household.name: model; fishing-net
household.title: model; fishing-net
household.reason: A woven bamboo/rattan fish trap (model of a fishing net/basket), a household/fishing tool plausibly made and used by Karen communities in Myanmar; museum credits Karen production directly.

garment.name: lannevaate
garment.title: lannevaate
garment.reason: This is a long narrow woven ikat-striped loincloth/waist cloth, explicitly documented as bought as Karen tribal handicraft from North Thailand, consistent with Karen weaving traditions (warp ikat bands, twisted fringe ends).

garment.name: blouse
garment.title: blouse
garment.reason: A woven cotton blouse with characteristic red/orange geometric bands and seed embellishment, explicitly attributed by the museum as made by Karen for an unmarried girl — a classic form of Karen traditional dress.

garment.name: robe
garment.title: robe
garment.reason: A man's tunic-style robe with white top and red striped/embroidered lower section, a form consistent with Karen traditional dress, and the museum attributes it directly to Karen makers.

garment.name: breeches
garment.title: breeches
garment.reason: Man's cotton breeches with striped weave, embroidery, and tasseled fringe, consistent with Karen (Red/Kayah) traditional men's dress, museum attributes to Karen (Red).

garment.name: jacket; cloth
garment.title: jacket; cloth
garment.reason: Coarse rust-red cotton cloth with thin multicoloured warp stripes, a square panel destined for a jacket, attributed by the museum as Karen-made — consistent with Karen handwoven striped cotton textiles.

garment.name: tunic
garment.title: tunic
garment.reason: Cotton tunic with red borders and horizontal striped weaving at the hem is a classic Karen women's/girl's tunic style, plain-woven with characteristic red banding. Matches typical Karen garment construction.

garment.name: turban
garment.title: turban
garment.reason: Black cotton turban with colorful tasseled ends, consistent with Karen women's traditional headwear in Myanmar; museum directly attributes it to Karen makers.

garment.name: coat
garment.title: coat
garment.reason: A long cotton coat with red striped/woven lower half and supplementary weft banding at the waist — a traditional Karen-style long tunic/coat, consistent with Karen dress conventions. The museum explicitly attributes production to the Karen.

garment.name: lon-gyi; sarong
garment.title: lon-gyi; sarong
garment.reason: A plain dark cotton sarong with yellow/green/red stripes, a classic Karen lungyi/sarong textile pattern, and the museum explicitly records it as made by Karen weavers. The image clearly shows the whole cloth.

garment.name: scarf
garment.title: scarf
garment.reason: The image shows a woven cotton scarf with fringed ends and striped embroidery bands in yellow, red/orange, and brown — a style consistent with Karen handwoven textiles from Myanmar, and the museum attributes it directly to Karen makers.

arms.name: arbetskniv, slida, kniv, knife
arms.title: arbetskniv, slida, kniv, knife
arms.reason: A sheathed knife (daukau/daukrau) with wooden handle, metal-ringed sheath, and red cord/tassel wrapping, collected directly from Karen villagers in Chomthong district, Chiangmai province — a documented traditional Karen object.

arms.name: armborstpil
arms.title: armborstpil
arms.reason: Crossbow arrow (armborstpil) collected by Dr. René Malaise among the Skaw Karen in Amherst district, Tenasserim, Burma — a documented traditional weapon/tool of the Karen people.

arms.name: cross-bow
arms.title: cross-bow
arms.reason: Wooden crossbow stock (part of), a traditional hunting weapon used by Karen people in Myanmar hill regions; museum explicitly attributes manufacture to Karen.

arms.name: trident
arms.title: trident
arms.reason: A bamboo-shafted rat-catching trident with a metal three-pronged head, a utilitarian tool/weapon used in Karen daily life, consistent with Karen material culture.

arms.name: koger
arms.title: koger
arms.reason: This is a woven quiver (koger/plamau) for crossbow bolts, made of bamboo/rattan with a woven holder, collected in Chomthong district, Chiengmai province — a documented Karen area of northern Thailand. It is a plausible Karen-made hunting implement.

instruments.name: drum
instruments.title: drum
instruments.reason: This is a classic bronze frog/Karen drum (bronze rain drum with star pattern tympanum and frog figures), a well-known instrument made and used by the Karen people of Myanmar. The form, cast bronze construction, and museum attribution all support this as a Karen instrument.

instruments.name: harpa
instruments.title: harpa
instruments.reason: A six-stringed harp (teiná) with carved wooden resonator and curved neck, collected in Chomthong district, Chiengmai province — a documented Karen harp type. Consistent with Karen material culture.

instruments.name: mandolin
instruments.title: mandolin
instruments.reason: A traditional handmade wooden box-lute (called "su") collected from a Karen village in Chiengmai province, Thailand, matching the Karen ethnicity claim.

instruments.name: sidblåst musikinstrument  ("flöjt" ?), Musikinstrument
instruments.title: sidblåst musikinstrument  ("flöjt" ?), Musikinstrument
instruments.reason: A side-blown wind instrument made of two bound wooden halves with rattan binding, collected in Chomthong district, Chiengmai province, and attributed to Karen people — a plausible traditional Karen horn/flute type, well made and clearly photographed.

instruments.name: buffelklocka
instruments.title: buffelklocka
instruments.reason: A bamboo buffalo bell (kauklo) with two wooden clappers, collected in Chomthong district, Chiangmai province, Thailand — a Karen-inhabited area — used by Karen herders for livestock; this is a traditional Karen-made object.

instruments.name: Buffelhorn, sidblåst buffelhorn
instruments.title: Buffelhorn, sidblåst buffelhorn
instruments.reason: A side-blown buffalo horn trumpet collected in Chomthong district, Chiang Mai province, explicitly noted as "karen" (Karen) in the field notes — a plausible traditional Karen signal/musical instrument.

instruments.name: jakthorn
instruments.title: jakthorn
instruments.reason: A curved animal horn fitted with a band near the mouthpiece, collected as a "jakthorn" (hunting horn) among the Sgaw Karen in the Tenasserim district of Burma by Malaise — a plausible Karen-made wind instrument.

instruments.name: oxklocka, Oxskälla
instruments.title: oxklocka, Oxskälla
instruments.reason: An "oxklocka" (ox bell) made of bamboo/wood with wooden clappers, collected from Skaw Karen people in the Amherst district of Tenasserim, Burma, during the Malaise research expedition — a traditional object used by Karen herders, consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

instruments.name: drum
instruments.title: drum
instruments.reason: This is a bronze frog drum (Karen "rain drum") with elephants, snails and frogs along the tympanum and sides, a well-documented instrument type specifically made and used by the Karen people of Myanmar.

photo.name: postcard
photo.title: postcard
photo.reason: Documentary studio/outdoor photo postcard of five young Karen women in traditional dress (woven tube skirts, white tunics, bead/metal neck rings and jewelry), captioned identifying them as Christian and "heathen" (animist) Karen girls — this is exactly the kind of documentary ethnographic photo that belongs.

ceramic.name: kärl, skål
ceramic.title: kärl, skål
ceramic.reason: A plain unglazed earthenware footed bowl used for curry and tea, collected at Kaungmaing in Burma and explicitly noted as used also by Red Karen and Zayein (Karenni) peoples — consistent with Karen-region domestic pottery.

ceramic.name: Lerskål, ryssja
ceramic.title: Lerskål, ryssja
ceramic.reason: A hand-built earthenware bowl, collected in Kawkareik district, Tenasserim, Burma, with the field note "Red Karen" — a handmade clay vessel plausibly made and used by Karen people, with incised decoration around the shoulder.

ceramic.name: kärl, skål
ceramic.title: kärl, skål
ceramic.reason: Simple earthenware bowl collected in Burma by Malaise, with museum note stating it was used also by Red Karen (Kayah) and Zarein, consistent with Karen use. Plain handmade pottery vessel, plausible for the region.

jewelry.name: örhänge
jewelry.title: örhänge
jewelry.reason: A pair of silver ear ornaments (cone-shaped pendants with hoops), collected by Malaise from Red Karen (Kayah) in Pekkong district, Burma — jewelry consistent with Karen dress.
